questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew that Amsterdam and The Netherlands in general were recognized for their media studies, and then Amsterdam attracted me, because the city is very similar to Copenhagen and the danish culture.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: As soon as I had all of the contact information on my host university and knew how their website was designed, I found it quite easy to find the information I needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The International Office from University of Amsterdam reached out to us through e-mail as everything at this point still was online.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was difficult, but I was also very lucky. I found it through a Facebook group, and just wrote to a bunch of people, and was lucky to find a room through the first interview I did. I would recommend to be aware of scammers of course, to be patient and also knowing that Dutch people usually post that they're searching for housemates pretty close to the move in date, so don't start looking until you have one month until moving in.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You get to live like a local, which is really nice. At the same time you are more isolated from the rest of the exchange students, as the majority live in student housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't even look at the student housing, so I don't really have an opinion about it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First, you had to kind of wish for the courses you wanted to have, and this was done through two different systems, which made it kind of difficult and confusing at times. Then you had to wait for some time to learn if you got the wished courses or not. If you didn't get the courses that you wished for, you had to apply through a second round.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We could write to the International Offices e-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was lucky and got the courses I wanted, but I know that wasn't the case for many students.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Even though you don't get the courses that you wished for there is always a solution, and the International Offices are really helpful.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The level was super high and challenging, higher than expected. Exchange students were also placed in the same courses as regular Dutch students, which also made the academic level higher, because we as exchange students had to catch up with what the regular students were taught. 

Nevertheless, the courses were super interesting and I really learned a lot!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Because the sizes of our courses were so high, we had a lot of lectures, where the teacher talked for two hours, and then the rest of the course was self-study.

Though, I also had one sociology course, where we also had one weekly tutorial group, where we discussed the texts more in depth, which was nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sociological Theory 2: Power, Culture, Identity
Topic The Role of Emotions in Political Communication
Topic Algorithmic Persuasion in Digital Society 
Topic Content Marketing
Topic Health Communication: From Theory to Practice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked Sociological Theory 2: Power, Culture, Identity and Topic Algorithmic Persuasion in Digital Society. I really liked the sociological theory course, because it really challenged my way of thinking, and the Algorithmic Persuasion was just really interesting and relevant for today's society.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I don't think I experienced any unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Public Transportation was more expensive than I thought, why you really need to get a bike in Amsterdam. Food wasn't cheap either. Coffee and beer was cheaper than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of different opportunities, but I just didn't use them.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You could take different kinds of drawing, painting and dancing classes. I think they also had a lot of sports activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really didn't really use any of the non-academic activities.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Amsterdam has a lot of nice museums, so I would definitely but their Museumkaart to save some money on entrance. Furthermore, I would visit some of the other Dutch cities like Rotterdam, The Hague, Leiden and Utrecht. I also took a trip to Paris doing my stay, which is only three hours away with train.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy as Dutch people are very similar to Danish people, and in general are very open and helpful. I also lived with three Dutch girls, which really helped me adjust to the Dutch culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open and don't be afraid of starting a conversation. The good thing about Dutch people is that they are very international and speaking English for them is very natural, so there is nothing to be scared off.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Biking in the city! I thought I was used to biking coming from Copenhagen, but the Dutch people bike in a completely different way, which wasn't always that logical.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and their helpfulness, it is rare to find people, who are so helpful.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be aware of the high academic level
Try to find some friends, who are taking the same courses as you, as you can study and support each other
Remember to explore and enjoy the amazing city

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything can seem super confusing at first, but UvA always has a solution, so you don't need to stress about anything.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social aspect and living in a different country, where you have to adapt to a completely new lifestyle.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The academic level and the workload, and of course also being away from your friends and family.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
